results.identification: A third‑party bullet‑point summary of the UK Conservative and Unionist Party’s 2017 General Election manifesto, “Forward, Together: Our Plan for a Stronger Britain and a Prosperous Future” (Theresa May). It derives from that manifesto.
results.evidence: The text explicitly labels itself “Conservative Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary,” and is filled with hallmark 2017 Tory pledges and phrases: “Strong and stable” leadership; leave the single market and customs union with a “Great Repeal Bill” and “no deal better than a bad deal”; reduce net migration to the “tens of thousands”; maintain 0.7% aid and defence ≥2% of GDP; retain Trident; move from the pensions Triple Lock to a Double Lock; means-test Winter Fuel Payments; social care reforms including home value in the means test and a £100,000 asset floor; an energy price “safeguard tariff” cap; HS2, Northern Powerhouse Rail and Heathrow expansion; T-levels and institutes of technology; UK Shared Prosperity Fund; a Digital Charter and right for young people to delete data at 18. These are all distinctive elements of the Conservative and Unionist Party’s 2017 general election manifesto under Theresa May (“Forward, Together: Our Plan for a Stronger Britain and a Prosperous Future”).

results.identification: An unofficial, supporter-made bullet‑point summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2017 general election manifesto (“For the Many, Not the Few”), not the official manifesto text.
results.evidence: The title line says “Labour Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words)”. The content matches signature 2017 UK Labour policies and slogans: “an economy for the many, not the few”; a £250bn National Transformation Fund; the Fiscal Credibility Rule; abolishing university tuition fees; public ownership of rail, energy networks, water and Royal Mail; £10 Living Wage by 2020; ending zero‑hours contracts; reversing NHS privatisation and adding >£30bn; jobs‑first Brexit with EU nationals’ rights; renewing Trident while keeping 0.7% aid. These are all core planks of Labour’s 2017 general election manifesto, For the Many, Not the Few.

results.identification: An unofficial, third‑party bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2017 General Election manifesto, compiled from the party’s official 2017 manifesto.
results.evidence: The header states “Liberal Democrats Manifesto 2017 – Summary,” and the bullet points align with distinctive 2017 UK Liberal Democrat pledges (e.g., a second EU referendum; 1p income tax rise for the NHS/social care; legal, regulated cannabis market; votes at 16 and STV; three‑boat reduced‑readiness nuclear deterrent; protections for Erasmus+, EHIC, and roaming; opposition to new grammar schools).

results.identification: A user‑generated bullet‑point summary of the Scottish National Party’s 2017 UK general election manifesto, posted as part of a ≤500‑word manifesto summaries thread on Politics Stack Exchange (community‑wiki).
results.evidence: The header reads “Scottish National Party Manifesto 2017 – Summary (≤500 words)”. The bullet points match SNP 2017 UK general election positions (e.g., scrapping Trident, opposing further Corporation Tax cuts, protecting EU nationals’ rights, Scotland’s right to choose an independence referendum post‑Brexit, returning the £190m convergence uplift to farmers, capping standard variable energy tariffs, no fox‑hunting). The “≤500 words” constraint and outline style are characteristic of a Politics Stack Exchange community‑wiki manifesto‑summary thread.

results.identification: A third‑party bullet‑point summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) 2017 UK general election manifesto, derived from UKIP’s official 2017 manifesto document (not the original manifesto text itself).
results.evidence: The heading explicitly says “UKIP Manifesto 2017 – Summary (under 500 words).” The bullet points list hallmark UKIP 2017 policies: six Brexit tests, reclaiming fisheries/200‑mile zone, bringing back blue passports, cutting foreign aid to 0.2% GNI, scrapping HS2 and the BBC licence fee, an Australian‑style points system with a pause on low‑skilled migration, banning face coverings, repealing the Human Rights Act and leaving the ECHR, creating an English Parliament and PR, and introducing a “Britdisc” for foreign vehicles.

results.identification: A non‑ideological bullet‑point summary of the UK Conservative and Unionist Party’s 2017 general election manifesto, ‘Forward, Together: Our Plan for a Stronger Britain and a Prosperous Future’ (Conservative Party, May 2017), compiled from the manifesto text.
results.evidence: Distinctive 2017 UK Conservative manifesto items: raise personal allowance to £12,500/£50,000 by 2020; cut corporation tax to 17%; energy price cap/safeguard tariff; leave single market and customs union with a Great Repeal Bill; social care reform including home value in means test with a £100,000 floor; end Leveson 2 and repeal Section 40; merge the SFO into the NCA; lift ban on new selective (grammar) schools; keep students in migration statistics and tighten student visas; create nine regional Trade Commissioners and reconvene the Board of Trade; UK Shared Prosperity Fund; Blue Belt marine protections; shale gas development with a new regulator; defence at ≥2% of GDP and +0.5% above inflation; aim for near‑zero‑emission cars/vans by 2050.

results.identification: A condensed summary of the UK Labour Party’s 2017 General Election manifesto, ‘For the Many, Not the Few,’ produced by the Labour Party (manifesto policy highlights).
results.evidence: References unique to UK Labour’s 2017 manifesto include: “£250bn National Transformation Fund…”, “National Investment Bank…”, “no income tax rise below £80k…”, “Fiscal Credibility Rule…”, “Return rail, energy networks, water and postal services to public ownership…”, “National Education Service… scrap tuition fees… restore maintenance grants”, “Living Wage ≥£10 by 2020”, “freedom of movement… end”, “recognise Palestine”, “renew nuclear deterrent while pursuing multilateral disarmament”, “Complete HS2… Crossrail of the North… Crossrail 2”, “ban fracking”, and “complete Leveson”.

results.identification: An ideology‑neutral bullet‑point summary of the UK Liberal Democrats’ 2017 General Election manifesto (“Change Britain’s Future”).
results.evidence: ‘Hold a referendum on the final EU deal, with an option to remain’; ‘Add 1p to Income Tax … ringfenced for NHS and social care’; ‘Regulate cannabis for adults’; ‘Votes at 16; STV for Westminster and local elections’; ‘Build 300,000 homes/year by 2022; at least 10 new garden cities’; ‘Young Person’s Bus Discount Card (16–21)’; ‘ban new diesel car/small van sales by 2025’; ‘maintain a minimum nuclear deterrent with reduced posture’. These are signature Liberal Democrat 2017 pledges.

results.identification: A neutral, bullet‑point summary of the Scottish National Party’s 2017 UK general election manifesto (“Stronger for Scotland”).
results.evidence: References specific to SNP positions and Scotland: cancelling nuclear weapons renewal (Trident), affirming the Scottish Parliament’s right to decide on a future independence referendum after Brexit terms are known, Scotland‑specific policies (free prescriptions and tuition, £2bn NHS Scotland increase, GM‑free status), oil and gas sector measures, opposition to Hinkley Point C, moratorium on fracking, devolution asks (immigration, employment law, agriculture/fisheries on repatriation), broadband to 100% by 2021, and EU‑related protections (Erasmus+, EMA, EHIC).

results.identification: A neutral, third‑party bullet‑point summary of the UK Independence Party (UKIP) 2017 General Election manifesto (‘Britain Together’), not the original manifesto text.
results.evidence: Distinctive UKIP 2017 policies appear throughout: banning face coverings in public; leaving the ECHR/ECJ and setting strict “six tests” for Brexit; restoring a 200‑mile Exclusive Economic Zone and creating a Fisheries Protection Force; abolishing the TV licence; repealing the Climate Change Act and leaving the Paris Agreement and EU ETS; cutting foreign aid to 0.2% and commissioning a 500‑bed hospital ship; near‑zero net migration with a five‑year moratorium on low‑skilled visas and requiring private medical insurance; abolishing the upper chamber, creating an English Parliament, PR for Commons, and citizen‑initiated referenda; scrapping HS2; FOBT £2 stake cap; hospital parking charges scrapped. These align with UKIP’s ‘Britain Together: The UKIP 2017 General Election Manifesto.’
